title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo's autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations when heavy traffic prevented them from reaching charging stations before their batteries depleted. At least a dozen vehicles, mostly Jaguar I-PACE models, remained stationary as a result. The system encountered conditions it was not designed to handle: congestion severe enough to trap vehicles in traffic for extended periods, and unplanned road closures that prevented normal routing.

This failure occurred in the deployment environment rather than in the vehicle control systems themselves. The vehicles functioned as designed, but the operational plan assumed sufficient battery reserves to reach charging infrastructure during normal to moderately disrupted traffic. A buffer between minimum battery charge and expected route completion, or a system to predict and preempt severe congestion by proactive repositioning, might have prevented the stranding.

One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks set off in the street, though whether this resulted from thermal damage, battery management failure, or another cause is not established. The company had previously paused San Francisco operations following a power outage, indicating repeated challenges with infrastructure resilience in this deployment.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations on Saturday after their batteries drained while stuck in heavy traffic. Video footage verified by NBC News showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, many of them Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets following a city-sponsored fireworks display near the Golden Gate Bridge. The company attributed the situation to major traffic disruptions, high volumes of travelers, and unplanned road closures that created unexpected congestion. Waymo's roadside assistance team worked to clear the vehicles, and the company stated it is evaluating ways to improve resilience during major traffic disruptions.

One Waymo vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks someone had set off, though no injuries were reported. A passenger described the vehicle continuing to drive as fireworks were lit in the street, while another witness reported spending nearly two hours in standstill traffic and said people were yelling at the Waymo vehicles because they had no drivers. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office indicated it would meet with stakeholders to discuss the incident and work toward improving the experience for future events. This represents another challenge for the company, which had paused San Francisco service briefly in December following a power outage.
